structure: A Playwright trace corpus from the tests repo (trade-imports-ins-tests) run against the workspace stack built from latest main: workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/traces-e2e/ holds one folder per test result, each with a trace.zip, plus report.json (the Playwright JSON report), which is the index: it maps every test to its spec file, line, describe block, project and trace folder. 191 results from 68 spec files: 178 in the animals project (tests/animals/e2e: 36 feature specs incl. 7 under features/address-book, 4 journey specs incl. 3 under journeys/persistence, 17 page specs, 1 visual spec) and 13 in the ins project (tests/ins/e2e/features: 7 address-book specs and 3 others). 183 passed first time, 6 were skipped (the five per-role 'offers no INS add link in stub mode' tests in addresses-read-only.spec.ts and 'offers no way to add an address in stub mode' in contact-address.spec.ts, all skipped because the full stack was running, yet each left a trace), and 2 timed out on the first attempt then passed on retry (notification-dashboard.spec.ts 'copies a submitted notification from its searched dashboard card' and transited-countries.spec.ts 'transit countries are optional: continuing with none saves and goes on'): both attempts have their own folder (the retry's ends -retry1). No test failed. Most traces are UI walks with DOM frame-snapshots (a page-control trace runs to about 30 actions and 60 snapshots); a few lifecycle and persistence traces are mainly API requests with few or no snapshots. Reading the traces: tim distil trace runs Playwright 1.62.1, and these traces were recorded by Playwright 1.64 (alpha), so 'open' refuses them with TraceVersionError. Each part agent unzips each trace.zip into its own part folder under distil/extract/trace-e2e.work/ and reads the N-trace.trace files (before/after actions, frame-snapshot DOM, log), N-trace.network (requests and responses) and test.trace (test steps and assertions) with jq; try 'tim distil trace ... -- open' first in case the viewer has been upgraded. The spec files under repos/trade-imports-ins-tests/tests/ name what each test asserts; the checkout may have moved on since the run, so where a spec and its trace disagree the trace wins. Cut: by spec file, grouped along the journey into 15 parts of 8 to 16 traces each: sign-in and headers, dashboard search and sort, the dashboard page and delete, the journey pages in order (origin and reason, commodities and consignment, identification and CPH, contact address, copied addresses, the picker and INS handshake, arrival and transit, transporters, documents), the hub, check your answers and view states, the lifecycle and persistence, and the ins project. Scope leaves out nothing in the folder: every result in report.json is in exactly one part. Being a trace corpus it is a lower bound: a page, branch or error no test walked is not in it.
